summary: PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25 extracts Richard–Yafaev, Generalised André–Pink–Zannier conjecture for Shimura varieties of abelian type (Publ. Math. IHÉS 141 (2025) 249–331). It has 41 items (1 library, 1 planned, 39 missing), four routes and six source issues. Its Part II (HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier) is well chosen and duplicates nothing. Two findings, one medium and one low, both from narrowings accepted hours before the review. (1, medium) Route 1 sends Masser–Wüstholz's uniform refinements of the Tate conjecture and the paper's uniform integral Faltings theorem (Theorem 4.7, Proposition 4.8) to R28.4. RS-06 had narrowed R28.4 to Faltings' qualitative Satz 3/4. Masser–Wüstholz's quantitative theory is owned by the accepted Faltings Part II 'Quantitative isogeny estimates' (PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 route 10), whose Masser–Wüstholz isogeny estimates these refinements rest on. So as routed the base layer would depend on its own Part II. The items should coalesce into that Part II. (2, low) Route 3 sends EGA IV-type flatness and integrality criteria over ℤ̄_p to SF.0, which RS-25 had narrowed to library reuse plus relative Spec and Proj. No stage plans them, and their only consumer is the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem in route 4's Part II.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (issue #1442, PR #1850) and its review by Claude Code cc-7b31c4 (issue #1443). This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither, nor PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 or its routes (I reviewed only the red team of Tsimerman, RT-PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18, which does not concern route 10's scope).

Read the four routes, their reasons and briefs, and the statuses of all 41 items in the repository at 287c7736. All five cited stage ids exist in the assembled atlas (2840 stages, 8007 edges). Three were narrowed by accepted proposals before this extraction's review: R28.4 by RS-06 (finding 1), SF.0 by RS-25 (finding 2) and RG2.4 by RS-31. RG2.4 still keeps 'Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their precise field/group ranges', so item 28 (hyperspecial models and the Cartan decomposition, planned at RG2.3/RG2.4) stands. R01.6 (route 2: Serre's ℓ-independence and Noot's specialization) is unchanged.

Route 4: its title reproduces the parent's current atlas title 'Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models'. The id HeckeOrbitsAndAndrePinkZannier appears in no other extraction. I found no stage planning Hecke-orbit heights, the uniform integral Tate hypothesis, p-adic Kempf–Ness or Seshadri's GIT over ℤ_p, as the review reported.

Masser–Wüstholz across extractions: PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 route 10 (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheoremsPartII, accepted) decomposes MW's Factorization estimates (isogeny degree bounds). This extraction's prerequisite [28] is MW's Refinements of the Tate conjecture, the uniform Galois-module consequence of those estimates (finding 1).

Library: the one library item (Goursat's lemma, mathlib:Subgroup.goursat, GroupTheory/Goursat.lean:128) was verified by the review. I found no library declaration for Nori's theory, Serre's complete reducibility, Kempf–Ness or the ℤ̄_p flatness criteria.

Source issues: did not re-verify E1–E6 on the page images. I read the review's account of E6 (Lemma 5.12's adjoint-centraliser identity), the one it calls material. No red-team finding depends on them.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25.result.json: route 1 (source FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems, stages ['FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4']) and its items PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25/11 (Masser–Wüstholz refinements of the Tate conjecture) and /12 (Theorem 4.7 and Proposition 4.8, uniform integral Faltings over fields of finite type)
findings.claim: Route 1 sends two uniform, quantitative refinements of Faltings' theorems to R28.4. Item 11 is Masser–Wüstholz's: for ℓ > M′, uniformly over open subgroups of bounded index, 𝔽_ℓ[U′(ℓ)] is semisimple with commutant End(A/K̄) ⊗ 𝔽_ℓ. Item 12 is the paper's Theorem 4.7 and Proposition 4.8: Ẑ[U′] has index ≤ M(A, K, d) in the centraliser, uniformly in U′, over fields of finite type. The accepted RS-06 narrowed R28.4 to the qualitative theorem: 'Own Faltings semisimplicity and integral End/Tate comparison as read in Satz 3/4'. The accepted Tsimerman route 10 created FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheoremsPartII, 'Part II: Quantitative isogeny estimates', 'because the accepted R28 source decomposition proves qualitative finiteness … not a dimension-uniform polynomial upper bound'. Masser–Wüstholz derive their refinements of the Tate conjecture from their isogeny estimates. Those estimates are the subject of that Part II, which decomposes their Factorization estimates. So as routed, the base layer R28.4 would need its own Part II's theorem, which inverts the rule that a Part II starts where its base stops. And the quantitative Masser–Wüstholz theory would be split between R28.4 and the Part II. Both RS-06 (13:29 UTC) and Tsimerman's route 10 (17:11 UTC) were accepted before this extraction's review (17:40 UTC, 23 September), which accepted route 1 unchanged.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25.result.json: route 3 (source SchemeAndStackFoundations, stages ['SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0']) and its item PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25/35 (Propositions 7.13–7.15)
findings.claim: Route 3 sends the paper's Propositions 7.13–7.15 to SF.0 as 'general scheme theory'. They are criteria for schemes of finite presentation over the non-noetherian valuation ring ℤ̄_p: X_red is flat iff every 𝔽̄_p-point lifts, iff the generic fibre is dense; ℤ̄_p-points lift along flat morphisms iff their reductions do; and integrality of points descends along integral morphisms. The accepted RS-25 narrowed SF.0 before this extraction's review. SF.0 now reuses 'the audited library carriers, morphisms, modules, gluing, pullbacks and morphism properties' and keeps only the relative Spec and general relative Proj constructions. Even before narrowing, SF.0 only stated flatness and the other properties 'as properties of named morphisms'. No stage in the atlas plans these criteria. Their only consumer is the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem (items 31–34), which route 4's Part II owns.
findings.evidence: Item 35 statement: 'For a closed X ⊆ 𝔸^n over ℤ̄_p of finite presentation, X_red is flat iff X(𝔽̄_p) = r_n(X(ℤ̄_p)) iff the generic fibre is dense iff no component lies in the special fibre (7.13); for flat π : X → Y, y ∈ Y(ℤ̄_p) lifts to X(ℤ̄_p) iff its reduction lifts (7.14); for integral π, x ∈ X(ℚ̄_p) is integral iff π(x) is (7.15).' Route 3 reason: 'SF.0 owns general scheme theory. The criteria for flatness by lifting of points … are general facts that the paper records for use in the p-adic Kempf–Ness theorem.' RS-25.result.json layers['SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0'].keeps: 'Reuse the audited library carriers, morphisms, modules, gluing, pullbacks and morphism properties. Keep the missing relative-Spec interface and general relative-Proj construction …'. REV-RS-25 committed 2026-09-23 13:09 UTC; REV-PAPER-RICHARD-YAFAEV-25 committed 17:40 UTC. Original SF.0 text: 'State flat, smooth, etale, proper, separated and finite-presentation hypotheses as properties of named morphisms.' A search of every stage description and narrowed 'keeps' for flatness or valuative criteria and lifting of points finds nothing that plans these statements.
